contexts.name: fleet-activity-feed
contexts.description: Cross-session activity tab that lists recently-active Claude Code sessions across all projects via fleet_recent_transcripts. Supports search by project name, files touched, tools used, or model, giving operators a searchable audit trail of what sessions have been doing across the whole fleet.

contexts.name: fleet-channel-lens-stream
contexts.description: The lens/filter system and flat event stream for a single team channel. lensModel defines five composable filter dimensions (kind, event family, callsign, team, free text) applied to the stream; LensStream renders the filter bar; Stream and StreamRow display the raw chronological log (no clustering) where each event is one row; StreamMemoryViews provides alternate memory-mode presentations (list/timeline/diff); useLensFeed applies the lens and manages paginated fetching.

contexts.name: fleet-channel-map
contexts.description: The Constellation map view inside the channel workspace that visualises team structure as a radial node layout. mapModel computes deterministic (FNV-1a jitter) polar coordinates for each persona node, groups them into angular sectors by role, and derives traffic edges from recent channel events; ChannelMap renders the SVG canvas; mapGlyphs provides the per-node persona icon glyphs and the animated traffic-edge arcs.

contexts.name: fleet-channel-workspace
contexts.description: The multi-team channel workspace that lets operators watch several teams' activity streams in parallel. MonitorChannelGrid is the 3-zone layout (team filter rail · merged stream · Quick Answer sidebar); ConversationComposer lets the user assign goals to teams; ConversationSidebar and related components display the clustered conversation view where consecutive steps collapse into single assignment or deliberation rows; conversationModel contains the pure clustering algorithm that keeps the timeline readable.

contexts.name: fleet-debug-tools
contexts.description: DEV-only debug recording tools that capture PTY output and session events to a JSON log file for post-mortem analysis. A footer pill shows record/stop status; a toolbar button arms or disarms recording. Only compiled/shown in dev builds (import.meta.env.DEV guarded).

contexts.name: fleet-footer-cluster
contexts.description: Persistent footer integration that surfaces a glanceable fleet status badge in the app's desktop footer — visible from any page without entering Fleet. The icon click opens the fullscreen grid overlay in place; a hover popover shows a full state-count breakdown and an escape hatch to navigate to the Fleet page.

contexts.name: fleet-grid-view
contexts.description: A compact control-panel read on the whole fleet where every persona is rendered as a small colour-coded square grouped by team. fleetGridModel folds the Monitor's seven-state pillar key down to four square states (running/failed/attention/idle) and provides stable, deterministic initials; FleetGridView renders the team groups; PersonaSquare is the individual coloured square with pulse animation for live-running personas; TeamBadge labels each team group.

contexts.name: fleet-harvest-reports
contexts.description: Run harvest panel that aggregates what a fleet run delivered once sessions declare FLEET:DONE. Reads run summaries and per-session reports from the registry without re-polling, displays session-level outcomes, and exports the complete report as Markdown for sharing or archiving.

contexts.name: fleet-live-overlay
contexts.description: The corner live-mode pop-up overlays that surface urgent channel events (review gates, failures, handoffs) as dismissible notification cards without requiring the Monitor to be open. liveModel defines the LiveMessage projection shape and shared visual helpers (author accent, avatar tint) so every overlay variant renders consistently; LiveCommsStack is the stacked notification queue; LiveChannelOverlay is the pop-up container; liveDevHarness provides a deterministic synthetic feed for development.

contexts.name: fleet-merged-feed
contexts.description: The merged multi-team feed surface that interleaves events from multiple channels into one unified timeline. mergedFeed provides the hook that merges items from several team channels sorted chronologically; MergedRow resolves how each TeamChannelItem is compactly displayed — choosing an icon, event label, tone class, and one-line summary — and renders the row that the channel workspace, live overlay, and any other surface share.

contexts.name: fleet-mobile-companion
contexts.description: Companion device pairing and mobile preview surfaces within Fleet Settings. FleetMobilePreview renders a phone-shaped frame showing how the session status looks on the mobile companion app; FleetPairDevice handles the QR code / pairing flow for connecting a mobile device to the desktop fleet.

contexts.name: fleet-monitor-shell
contexts.description: The full-screen fleet monitor overlay that fuses all persona signals into one control surface. PersonaMonitor is the top-level view, hosting three switchable view modes (fleet columns, grid, channels) and a sliding triage drawer; monitorModel contains the pure state machine that derives card colour, pillar visuals, and fleet-wide rollup from live process/review/message data; useMonitorData polls reviews, messages, and health feeds and wires them into a single MonitorData object consumed by the view.
contexts.api_surface: listManualReviews, updateManualReviewStatus, dispatchReviewAction, listMessages, markMessageRead (via api/overview)

contexts.name: fleet-page-shell
contexts.description: Top-level Fleet plugin entry point that hosts the three internal tabs (Sessions, Activity, Settings) within a Dev Tools sub-panel. Bootstraps the app-wide session listener so the footer status cluster and grid overlay work on any page, not just when Fleet is open. Also exposes a grid-layout math module for density-scaled terminal columns.

contexts.name: fleet-session-grid
contexts.description: Primary Sessions tab showing the live list of Claude Code sessions with per-session controls (spawn, kill, hibernate, wake, broadcast). Manages the active-session selection, session list filtering by state, and the sub-panel that hosts the terminal pane, insights, or harvest report. Integrates the skill library drawer and Athena attention wiring.
contexts.api_surface: fleet_spawn_session, fleet_headless_session, fleet_kill_session, fleet_hibernate_session, fleet_wake_session, fleet_write_input

contexts.name: fleet-session-insights
contexts.description: Per-session analytics sub-panel shown alongside or instead of the live terminal in the grid. Displays transcript-derived insights, context-pill labels for the session's active workspace, and a token/cost summary bar. Helps operators understand what a session has been doing without reading the raw terminal output.

contexts.name: fleet-session-operations
contexts.description: Modals and hooks for the three session-level operations the operator initiates: spawning a new session with a pre-seeded task prompt (including headless/stream-json mode), broadcasting a PTY write to multiple sessions at once, and scanning OS process tables for orphaned Claude processes not tracked by the fleet registry.

contexts.name: fleet-session-status
contexts.description: Pure business-logic layer that classifies sessions by attention level (waiting, stale, failed, athena, none), derives Athena prompt templates for stale sessions, and filters companion approvals to those targeting a specific session's PTY. Also holds the state-metadata palette (colors, labels, ordering) shared across every status indicator in the UI.

contexts.name: fleet-sessions-repo
contexts.description: Repositories for Fleet multi-agent orchestration sessions — tracks active CLI agent sessions spawned by Fleet, their status, output streaming state, and decision history. Fleet decisions records capture the choices made by orchestrating agents for audit and replay purposes.

contexts.name: fleet-settings
contexts.description: Fleet Settings tab covering hook installation/uninstallation diagnostics, terminal appearance preferences (font size, copy-on-select, theme), auto-hibernate policy, live slot cap, state cutoff thresholds, and the OS process scanner for finding orphaned Claude processes. Central configuration surface for the whole fleet plugin.

contexts.name: fleet-skill-library
contexts.description: In-Fleet skill browser and installer giving operators inline access to the Claude Code skill library (project-scoped and global ~/.claude/skills) without leaving the session aggregator. Supports search, favorites, recently-opened tracking, file preview, install/uninstall, and pre-filling the broadcast modal with a /skill-name invocation.
contexts.api_surface: dev_tools skill APIs (list, install, uninstall, preview)

contexts.name: fleet-terminal-manager
contexts.description: Singleton xterm.js lifecycle manager keyed by session ID. Creates, parks (LRU up to 6), and disposes Terminal instances so switching sessions or opening the grid overlay re-attaches the same buffered terminal instead of rebuilding it. Handles PTY output hydration, WebGL renderer loading, copy-on-select, right-click paste, and per-session IPC subscription/unsubscription.

contexts.name: fleet-terminal-overlay
contexts.description: Fullscreen terminal grid overlay portaled to document.body, rendering every live session as a tile above the current page without navigating away. Tiles show either a live terminal (for sessions needing attention or the focused session) or a cheap status block for autonomous sessions. Hosts the per-tile Athena copilot bar for approve/reject of AI-proposed PTY writes.

contexts.name: fleet-tests
contexts.description: Vitest test suite for the fleet plugin covering attention classification logic, session scope ordering, status dot rendering, broadcast modal behavior, debug log controls, footer icon behavior, overlay rendering, skill library drawer, and harvest markdown generation.

contexts.name: fleet-triage-columns
contexts.description: The default fleet view that organises personas into team-scoped project columns, showing only 'actionable' cards (failed, pending review, input-required, draft-ready). triageModel defines the isActionable predicate and derives the priority-ordered action badge set (review severity, input gate, draft ready, unread messages) for each persona card; MonitorProjectColumns renders the column grid and PersonaGlyph the per-card glyph in the compact pillar.
